title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: Hold: the plugin installation row supplies a blocking operation, not an installation operation. The spending-control path also stops at the dashboard rather than taking administrators to the spending limits. The roadmap dates, preview qualification, consumption model and Dataverse update operations are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans access to Business Applications through Work IQ in Cowork and Business Skills for end-to-end business processes.
claims.quote: Users can access Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork and use Business Skills to complete end-to-end business processes grounded in their enterprise data and apps.

claims.claim: The roadmap products are Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365), Microsoft Dataverse and Work IQ.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Dataverse", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: Administrators can install the plugin for All users or Specific users and groups.

claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: After skills are created and activated, Copilot Chat, Cowork and connected agents can discover and use the skills accessible to the user.
claims.quote: After you create and activate business skills in your environment, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ MCP is generally available.
claims.quote: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Microsoft Copilot Studio is generally available.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; changes
claims.claim: Learn documents Cowork access as public preview, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Access through Cowork is available in public preview.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: All users is the default tenant audience option.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.claim: The previously documented November 2026 schedule for enabling existing environments has been deferred.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Cowork and Work IQ respect the user's existing business-data permissions and do not grant additional access.
claims.quote: Work IQ respects your existing Power Platform security permissions. ... Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: For US tenants using FedRAMP-accredited environments, enabling Work IQ might send data outside the FedRAMP authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: Plugin connection includes choosing credentials and entering the sign-in approval number in Authenticator.
claims.quote: Select your credentials. A number appears to approve your sign in request. ... Enter the number in the Authenticator app.

claims.claim: Business skills are user-owned by default.
claims.quote: Skills are user-owned by default.

claims.claim: A business skill can be shared with everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Security-role-based skill access requires both the shared-with security role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ can create and update business records.
claims.quote: For example, ask Work IQ to list records from an app view, show the details of a record, create a record with the values in your prompt, or update an existing record.

claims.claim: Users review proposed values and explicitly confirm a data-changing operation before submission.
claims.quote: For an operation that changes data, review the proposed values, make any needed changes, and explicitly confirm the operation before it's submitted.

claims.claim: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.
claims.quote: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.

claims.claim: Users can create and update skills through Copilot or a connected agent.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server:

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing skills with repeatable scenarios before sharing them broadly.
claims.quote: Test each skill with a repeatable scenario before you share it broadly.

claims.claim: Record creation and updates are unavailable when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange or OnSave handlers.
claims.quote: You can't create or update a record when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange, or OnSave event handlers.

claims.claim: Custom controls and subgrids are unsupported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: The Business skills page does not currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business context and Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task are attributed to Cowork consumption.
claims.quote: Business context accessed through Cowork contributes to Cowork consumption. ... Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, cost; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The consumption licensing model and variable cost rating use Copilot Credits as the meter.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity packs can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Direct Work IQ API use is reported separately and its total is not a Business Applications-only breakdown.
claims.quote: Direct calls through the Work IQ API are reported under Work IQ API. ... Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so a prompt is not necessarily a fixed-price operation.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's documentation publishes no per-task Copilot Credit rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork per-task rate; Cowork Business apps plugin licensing pricing per task rate. Opened cowork-work-iq, understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations and Work IQ API licensing; reviewed Cowork FAQ billing search excerpt. No fixed per-task rate found.

claims.claim: Learn names no separate license for this particular plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps license; Cowork Business apps plugin licensing pricing. Opened cowork-work-iq, cowork-manage-plugins, plugins/cost-considerations and Work IQ API licensing. General user-license prerequisites exist; no distinct plugin license found.

claims.claim: The experience can vary with the organization's apps, licenses, policies and available services.
claims.quote: Some experiences might vary based on your organization's apps, licenses, policies, and available services.

claims.claim: Spending policies covering Cowork can impose policy-level and per-user consumption limits.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API. ... Set policy and per-user limits ... Limit monthly consumption for selected user groups and the services covered by their policies.

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during consumption-based previews.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the Power Platform environment, model-driven app and business data in the request.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps must be Default or On.
claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting (m365copilotmodelappenabled) must be set to Default or On.

claims.claim: Learn names AI Administrator for managing Work IQ experience availability in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Learn names Power Platform Administrator for the environment and application-access settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator to configure environment settings.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Plugin installation is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > Business apps (preview) > Install.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... In the Name column, select Business apps (preview). ... In the Business apps (preview) panel, select the Install button.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block is the automation counterpart of whether the plugin is installed for users.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and remove the call from the rendered installation row: blocking usage does not install or uninstall a plugin. Replace the API clause in its note with 'Installation automation is not yet documented.' The general blocking operation may remain described separately in the governance prose.

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The printed package-block operation exists as a general beta API operation.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Microsoft does not specifically confirm that the named Business apps (preview) plugin appears in the Package Management API inventory.
claims.quote: Searched: Business apps copilotPackage install block Cowork; Business apps Package Management API. Opened Package Management overview, package block, cowork-work-iq and cowork-manage-plugins. General plugin coverage exists; no named catalog-entry confirmation found.

claims.claim: The tenant audience setting is at Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. ... In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: No API for the tenant Business Applications audience setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data in Work IQ Graph API tenant audience setting; Work IQ Set-TenantSettings Copilot. Opened default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; reviewed Graph-related search results. No operation for this audience setting found.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. ... Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Locate Work IQ. ... Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: No API for the environment Work IQ switch is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ organization PowerShell environment setting Power Platform API enable; Dataverse intelligence API organization enable setting; Work IQ environment pac admin settings. Opened participation and organization table reference; searched its Work IQ/intelligence/Copilot columns.

claims.claim: App Access is enabled through Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable.
claims.quote: Select Security > Identity & access. ... Select App Access Control. ... Select the environment in which you want to enable app access. ... Select Enable, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Keep the feature-specific path, but add to the existing note: 'After saving, return to the environment and select the applications to block. The general App Access guide instead describes Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled, then selecting an application and Block: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/control-app-access-environment.'

claims.claim: An application access record can be updated with PATCH https://<organization>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<applicationid>).
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /applications(applicationid)

claims.claim: The writable access property uses 0 for Allowed and 1 for Blocked.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/applications ... access ... Application Access ... 0 | Allowed ... 1 | Blocked

claims.claim: The general App Access documentation requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Verify that your environment is a managed environment ... Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management is the complete path to the control setting how much Cowork can consume.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: ... Spending limits
claims.fix: Replace controls[4].ui.path and its rendered path with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits' and set its docs URL to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits#edit-spending-policy. Add that page to sources. The current path stops at the dashboard and omits the Configuration tab and the actual limits control.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending policies.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: Spending policies cover selected users and services and support policy-level and per-user limits.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: The beta spending-policy update accepts periodLimit and perUserLimit in the request body.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Skills are deactivated through Power Apps > environment > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps and select your environment. ... select More, and then select Business skills. ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu.

claims.claim: PATCH /skills(<skillid>) can change a skill's state using statecode and statuscode.
claims.quote: SetState ... PATCH /skills(skillid) ... Update the statecode and statuscode properties.

claims.claim: statecode 1 and statuscode 2 identify an inactive skill.
claims.quote: statecode Choices/Options ... 1 | Label: Inactive DefaultStatus: 2 InvariantName: Inactive ... statuscode Choices/Options ... 2 | Label: Inactive State:1

claims.claim: Deactivation stops discovery and use of an active skill without deleting its content or version history.
claims.quote: To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill: ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate ... Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.

claims.claim: The Business skills page provides Share for a selected skill.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu.

claims.claim: The whole Work IQ MCP server can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether blocking the whole Work IQ MCP server also stops this Cowork plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Work IQ MCP Block plugin server; Business Applications Work IQ MCP Cowork block dependency. Opened cowork-work-iq, manage-ai-experience-access and Business Applications overview; no explicit plugin dependency or block-propagation statement found.

claims.claim: Enabling an experience does not grant access to business data.
claims.quote: Enabling an experience doesn't grant access to business data.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic data access; App Access controls application access, including Cowork.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment. ... Work IQ participation settings serve a different purpose and don't prevent agentic access.

claims.where: Governance controls; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Plugin deployment, tenant audience, environment participation and application access are separate configuration decisions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Cowork ... Administrators configure the Microsoft 365 audience. Power Platform administrators and makers configure participating environments and apps.

claims.claim: Specific groups is an available tenant audience option.
claims.quote: To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups, and then add or remove groups.

claims.claim: No users is an available tenant audience option that turns off access for everyone.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users.

claims.claim: The quickstart uses slightly different wording for the audience setting label.
claims.quote: Open the setting for Business Applications in Work IQ available to Copilot in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: An application's Allowed or Blocked status is distinct from enabling environment-level App Access enforcement.
claims.quote: If you set some apps to Allowed or Blocked, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to Disabled. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: Preview behavior is subject to change.
claims.quote: This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.
